meta.move: Weak path: leads with the checker, calls Owen a cheater, threatens the record
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, and I'd like to know who decided Owen gets a zero and whether anyone heard from him before it went into the gradebook. He found out on his phone, in the middle of a class.
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%. That's why it's a zero.

A machine's guess, and the company that sells it says in its own guide not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student. Your school's procedure says the same thing at 4.3: software alone does not establish a concern. So what else do you have, Hale, or is the checker the whole case?
Honestly, your son cheated. The software is very reliable.

My child doesn't cheat, and he never lies. You just called him a cheater with nothing in front of you but a percentage, and I'm writing that down. When we're done here I'm going upstairs to the principal.
If you keep fighting this, I'll have to put it on his permanent record.

You're threatening his record because his mother asked questions, and I'm writing that down word for word. Your own procedure says a first concern gets a supervised reassessment and nothing goes on file; only repeated concerns go to administration. Is this a first concern, Hale, yes or no?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, an apology for entering it without hearing from Owen or calling me first, and confirmation that nothing about this goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed, and she was headed to the principal after the teacher called Owen a cheater and threatened his record.
What moved her: nothing.
